notes:
SDSS J090745.0+024507: explicitly a previously discovered HVS in T:p1-b8, with a radial-velocity statement over twice the Galactic escape value; recorded as follow_up, not a new candidate.
HE 0437-5439: called an HVS, used as a mass benchmark (T:p2-b1), and discussed as a possible merger product (T:p4-b15); no explicit velocity/escape comparison is given here, so follow_up status relies on the paper's HVS definition (T:p1-b8) and the cited prior identification (T:p4-b15).
US 708: called an HVS and discussed as a possible merger product in T:p4-b15; no explicit velocity/escape comparison is given here, so follow_up status relies on the paper's HVS definition (T:p1-b8) and the cited prior identification (T:p4-b15).
SDSS J090745.0+024507 / HE 0437-5439 / US 708: the abstract at T:p1-b5 reports seven HVSs, but only these three are individually identified in the supplied text; the remaining four cannot be expanded and are omitted.

SDSS J090745.0+024507: The paper only reports two quantities for the target star SDSS J090745.0+024507: an approximate heliocentric distance of ∼110 kpc and a radial velocity of 853 ± 12 km/s. The paper also gives its estimated mass (3 M☉), which is not among the requested quantities.

HE 0437-5439: The paper mentions HE 0437-5439 only as an HVS whose estimated mass (~10 M_sun) motivated one of the simulated binary mass configurations, and (citing Edelmann et al. 2005) as possibly the merger of two 4 M_sun stars (T:p2-b1, T:p4-b15). No values for any of the target quantities (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) are reported for this star. The only HVS with a reported radial velocity is SDSS J090745.0+024507 (853 ± 12 km/s), not the target star.

US 708: US 708 is mentioned only in T:p4-b15, where the paper states that Hirsch et al. (2005) suggest it is a subluminous O star and possibly the merger of two helium-core white dwarfs. The paper reports no numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for US 708.
